title: Darden School (UVA): Upside Inflation Risks, Next Move Needs More Data
summary: In a full outlook speech plus Q&A at UVA's Darden School, Jefferson says inflation is too high, has exceeded 2% for more than five years, and that risks to his inflation forecast are tilted to the upside (energy, AI-driven demand), while growth and employment risks are roughly balanced. In the Q&A he sharpens the mandate prioritization: with the economy at maximum employment and resilient, it is 'appropriate that we're focused on the inflation side at this time', he does not take anchored long-run expectations for granted and says the Fed must be prepared to do the work necessary to validate them; he also frames the AI boom as a demand-supply imbalance that feeds inflation, while staying open on whether AI raises r*. He supported the September hike, but gives no further-tightening signal: future adjustments depend on trends in the data, he notes the further rise in yields since September, and the committee's judgment 'may take more time'. Versus July, when he only floated reconsidering the stance if inflation did not cool soon, he has endorsed the hike and moved explicitly to the inflation side of the mandate, yet remains patient on the next move, short of Barr's or Williams's call for more.

key_quotes.quote: While I view the risks to both economic activity and employment as roughly balanced at this point, I see upside risks to inflation.
given the strength in the labor market and the resilience of the economy overall, it is my view that it's appropriate that we're focused on the inflation side at this time.
key_quotes.context: Q&A, on when to stop looking through supply shocks; max employment gives latitude to focus on inflation.

key_quotes.quote: I for a minute don't take it for granted that those longer term inflation expectations will stay around our 2% target.
My colleagues and I will need to come to our own judgment, which may take more time.
key_quotes.context: After noting that yields across the term structure rose further since September; on the next policy move.
